narrative.lead: Sullivanesque in style. The architect's other surviving San Francisco skyscraper is the Westinghouse Building at Second and Natoma Streets, designed in 1907 for Knickerbocker & Bostwick.

historical_record.description: Recorded in the city's 2008 survey of the Transit Center District, adopted in 2012, as a contributor to the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District.
Built as the Morton Cook Building.
Designed by architect John Cotter Pelton Jr., who returned to San Francisco commissions after 1906 and helped rebuild the downtown and South of Market.
